The friend who mentioned this was likely thinking of hyperthyroidism (an overactive thyroid). When your thyroid produces too many hormones, it dials your metabolism up to a high gear, which can make it incredibly difficult to gain weight—or cause you to drop weight rapidly—even if you are eating a high-calorie diet consistently.

Your April 2022 Marek Health panel actually checked the core markers needed to evaluate your thyroid function. If you want to pull up your specific lab results to see where you fell, here are the three specific markers that were included in that test and what they do:

  • TSH (Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone): This is a signal sent from your brain to your thyroid, telling it how hard to work. If your thyroid is overactive (hyperthyroidism), your TSH will usually drop incredibly low because your brain is trying to tell your thyroid to shut down production.
  • Free T4 (Thyroxine): This is the main physical hormone your thyroid gland produces.
  • Free T3 (Triiodothyronine): This is the active form of the hormone that your body's tissues actually use to regulate your metabolism. In cases of hyperthyroidism, both Free T4 and Free T3 are typically elevated above the normal reference ranges.

Because that specific panel is from a few years ago, it's important to know that thyroid function can absolutely change over time. If you find that this rapid weight fluctuation and high metabolic rate are accompanied by other subtle symptoms—like feeling unusually hot when others are comfortable, a racing heartbeat, or feeling jittery/anxious—it is well worth sharing this observation with a doctor. However, before deciding if it's a healthy or sustainable experiment for your body, it is important to weigh the practical safety factors and potential downsides:

The Long-Term Considerations & Safety

  • Frequent Injections: L-Carnitine requires a large volume to be effective, meaning protocols often call for daily or near-daily intramuscular injections. Long-term, frequent pinning of the same muscle groups can lead to localized tissue irritation, sterile abscesses, or scar tissue formation if proper rotation and sterile technique aren't strictly maintained.
  • Kidney & Liver Load: While naturally occurring, processing high concentrations of synthetic compounds puts an extra filtration workload on your kidneys and liver. .
  • The Insulin Requirement: For intramuscular L-Carnitine to actually be absorbed into the muscle cells effectively, it generally requires an insulin spike. This means you typically have to consume a high-carbohydrate meal or fast-acting sugars alongside the injection. For a high-mileage runner, timing this around your training is manageable, but it requires careful planning to avoid unwanted blood sugar crashes.
  • Bypassing TMAO Risks: One major health benefit of the injectable route over the oral route is that it bypasses the gut microbiota entirely. High doses of oral carnitine are converted by gut bacteria into TMAO (trimethylamine N-oxide), a compound heavily linked to cardiovascular risk. Injecting completely avoids this specific issue, making it a safer option for your heart.

Is it a "Healthy" Thing to Try?

If your primary goal is optimizing cellular recovery and stamina without overloading your endocrine system with synthetic hormones, a high-quality, medically supervised course of injectable L-Carnitine can be a relatively safe tool. , you won't risk crashing your baseline hormone health.

Shifting your focus to marathon running changes the game for injectable L-Carnitine. While bodybuilders use it to up-regulate androgen receptors for muscle growth, endurance athletes value it for a completely different biological reason: mitochondrial glycogen sparing.

How L-Carnitine Alters Endurance Performance

When you are running deep into a marathon, your body burns through its limited glycogen (carbohydrate) stores, eventually leading to "hitting the wall." L-Carnitine acts as a shuttle that transports long-chain fatty acids directly into your cellular mitochondria to be burned for fuel.

By drastically improving your body's ability to oxidize fat at higher running intensities, it allows you to rely on your almost limitless fat stores for energy, "sparing" your precious glycogen for later in the race. It also helps minimize lactic acid buildup, which dramatically cuts down your recovery time between heavy training runs.

Assessing Your Current Stack: Creatine + Turkesterone

Taking a passive approach with a daily morning mix of creatine and turkesterone to support your active work is a solid, low-maintenance routine, but there are a few nuances to consider if your priority is long-term health and sustainability:

1. Creatine: The Gold Standard

This is completely safe and excellent for daily use. For a runner, it provides rapid ATP (energy) regeneration for your active work and sprint finishes, helps with cellular hydration, and protects against muscle wasting during heavy mileage.

2. Turkesterone: The Caveats

Turkesterone (an ecdysteroid, or plant hormone) has exploded in popularity because it’s marketed as a way to boost protein synthesis without suppressing your natural testosterone or stressing your liver like traditional synthetics.

However, if you want to be smart and sustainable, you should approach it with a healthy dose of skepticism:

  • The Quality Control Issue: Because it is a loosely regulated herbal supplement, third-party lab testing has frequently shown that many commercial brands don't actually contain the amount of active turkesterone listed on the label—or worse, are padded with other compounds.
  • The Lack of Human Data: Almost all promising data on turkesterone comes from rodent or in vitro studies. There is very little robust human clinical data proving its long-term safety or definitive efficacy.
  • Organ Health: While generally thought to be mild, emerging case reports have occasionally linked incredibly high or prolonged doses of unregulated ecdysteroids to unexpected liver stress or drug-induced liver injury.

The Sustainable Path Forward

If your goal is overall well-being and safe muscle preservation, your current passive routine is fine, but it’s always wise to cycle off herbal extras like turkesterone every 8 to 12 weeks to give your liver and kidneys a baseline break.
